newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury confident despite strong pound.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury confident despite strong pound.

text.p: Food and drinks group Cadbury Schweppes Plc on Wednesday reported a 16 percent increase in profits for 1996 and said it was confident of more growth in 1997 despite a stronger pound.
Pre-tax profits for the 52 weeks to December 28 rose to 592 million pounds from 511 million in the previous year. Sales were up seven percent to 5.12 billion pounds from 4.78 billion.
Chairman Dominic Cadbury said 1996 had produced record turnover, profits, margins and earnings and generated 137 million pounds ($221.1 million) free cash flow.
"At this early stage of the year we are confident of further growth and success in 1997 despite the impact of the stronger pound," he said in a statement.

In the United States, where Cadbury is number three in soft drinks, the company said Dr Pepper continued to outperform the market and the relaunch of 7 UP was encouraging. The group said the sale of its 51 percent interest in Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages, completed last month for 623 million pounds, gave it more freedom to develop both its soft drinks and confectionery interests.
